questions.q: What HTTP status code does Cosmos DB return when a request would exceed the container's provisioned RU/s budget for that second?
options: 429 (Request rate is large)
500 (Internal Server Error)
403 (Forbidden)
409 (Conflict)
questions.explain: A 429 is Cosmos DB's throttling response, accompanied by an x-ms-retry-after-ms header telling the client how long to wait.

questions.q: What do Cosmos DB SDKs do by default when they receive a 429?
options: Automatically retry the request after the suggested delay
Immediately crash the application
Permanently disable the connection
Silently drop the request with no error
questions.explain: Built-in retry-on-429 logic is enabled by default in every Cosmos DB SDK, which is why occasional 429s under bursty load are often invisible to the app.

questions.q: Where can you find the exact RU cost of a specific Cosmos DB operation?
options: The RequestCharge property returned on every response, success or failure
It cannot be determined per-operation, only at the account level
Only by contacting Microsoft support
In the container's indexing policy
questions.explain: Every response carries its RU cost directly, making it the starting point for any RU investigation — comparable to checking STATISTICS IO in SQL Server.

questions.q: A container's overall Normalized RU Consumption shows only 40%, but the app is seeing frequent 429s. What's the most likely explanation?
options: A hot partition — one physical partition is being hit disproportionately while overall usage looks fine
Cosmos DB is malfunctioning and needs a support ticket
The account has run out of storage
The consistency level is set too strictly
questions.explain: RU/s is split evenly across physical partitions; an uneven partition key can overload one partition while the container-level average still looks healthy.

questions.q: What is the real fix for a hot partition caused by a poor partition key choice, per this lesson?
options: Revisit the partition key design so traffic spreads evenly, rather than just raising RU/s
Simply increase the provisioned RU/s until the 429s stop
Switch the entire account to a different consistency level
Disable indexing on the container
questions.explain: Adding more RU/s raises the ceiling for every partition, including ones that were never the bottleneck, and wastes money — the real fix is a better partition key.
